nodes.label: Client HTML Shell (#root mount, Inter font, logos.svg favicon)
nodes.norm_label: client html shell (#root mount, inter font, logos.svg favicon)
nodes.rationale: Single-page entry that mounts the React app at #root via /src/main.jsx and preconnects to Google Fonts to load Inter before first paint.

nodes.label: Serverless Cold Start Latency
nodes.rationale: A first request taking 3+ seconds is an expected, harmless cold start of the Vercel serverless function, not a bug.

nodes.label: AI Panel Component
nodes.rationale: Surfaces inbox insights, follow-ups, suggested actions, meeting extraction, and AI confidence in one docked panel.

nodes.label: Four-Panel Workspace Layout (Sidebar | List | Detail | AI Panel)
nodes.norm_label: four-panel workspace layout (sidebar | list | detail | ai panel)
nodes.rationale: Gmail-inspired productivity layout: desktop shows the full four panels, tablet collapses the sidebar and docks the AI panel, mobile degrades to a single-column flow with a drawer and bottom navigation.

nodes.label: Omni Platform Design System (palette, radii, 4px spacing rhythm)
nodes.norm_label: omni platform design system (palette, radii, 4px spacing rhythm)
nodes.rationale: Constraining to a fixed Omni palette, an allowed radius set (4/6/8/12/16/pill), and a strict 4px spacing rhythm enforces visual consistency across the app.

nodes.label: AI Processing Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Full email content is fetched, then summarization, priority detection, meeting extraction, and reply generation run before structured data is stored for the frontend smart inbox.

nodes.label: Future Improvements Roadmap (RAG memory, vector DB, semantic search, agents)
nodes.norm_label: future improvements roadmap (rag memory, vector db, semantic search, agents)

nodes.label: High-Level Architecture (React frontend, Express REST API, Google APIs, AI, MongoDB)
nodes.norm_label: high-level architecture (react frontend, express rest api, google apis, ai, mongodb)

nodes.label: React + Vite Template Notes
nodes.rationale: The React Compiler is intentionally not enabled on this template because of its impact on dev and build performance.

nodes.label: Saarthi Mail Frontend Design System Doc
nodes.norm_label: saarthi mail frontend design system doc
nodes.rationale: The UI should feel calm, intelligent, modern, and hackathon-winning while maintaining strong usability and smooth motion.

nodes.label: Saarthi Mail
nodes.rationale: Traditional email clients are passive; Saarthi Mail combines AI reasoning, email intelligence, workflow automation, and productivity tooling into one platform that acts as an active assistant.

nodes.label: MongoDB Atlas Open IP Allowlist for Vercel
nodes.norm_label: mongodb atlas open ip allowlist for vercel
nodes.rationale: Vercel egress IPs rotate, so 0.0.0.0/0 is added to the Atlas allowlist; production-grade setups should use the Atlas Vercel integration or a NAT gateway instead.

nodes.label: Demo Write Blocking (blockDemoWrites)
nodes.rationale: ensureAuthenticated guards /api/mail and /api/gmail; blockDemoWrites returns 403 for demo sessions on mail create/update/delete and calendar create, and Gmail sync is disabled while message reads serve the seeded Mongo copy. AI summaries, suggested replies, and meeting detection still run live — only write-back is suppressed so the seeded inbox stays pristine for the next visitor.
nodes.source_location: Section 10, What the demo cannot do

nodes.label: DNS_SERVERS Resolver Override
nodes.rationale: Node/c-ares queries resolvers directly instead of the OS stub resolver, so a stale 127.0.0.1 nameserver (from a local DNS filter or inactive VPN) makes Atlas SRV lookups fail while browsers still work. DNS_SERVERS points server/src/config/dns.js at working resolvers; left unset on Vercel where DNS works.

nodes.label: dotenv Working-Directory Pitfall
nodes.rationale: server/server.js calls a bare dotenv.config() which resolves relative to the working directory, and npm run dev runs from server/, so a repo-root .env is never loaded — producing an empty MONGO_URI and a connect-mongo assertion at boot.

nodes.label: Env-Driven URL Configuration (CLIENT_URL, VITE_API_BASE_URL, GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL)
nodes.rationale: All cross-origin URLs (CORS origin, OAuth callback, post-login redirect, API base) come from environment variables rather than hardcoded hosts, so the same code deploys to localhost, *.vercel.app, or a custom domain with only env changes. Mismatched CLIENT_URL causes CORS failures; missing GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL sends OAuth back to localhost.

nodes.label: Idempotent Demo Inbox Seeding (npm run seed:demo)
nodes.norm_label: idempotent demo inbox seeding (npm run seed:demo)
nodes.rationale: The demo reads real Email documents owned by DEMO_USER_EMAIL. The seed script deletes every existing demo-owned email first, making it idempotent and re-runnable any time the demo inbox needs resetting.

nodes.label: MongoDB-Backed Session Store (connect-mongo)
nodes.rationale: Vercel serverless functions have no sticky sessions and no in-memory state across cold starts, so Express sessions must be persisted in MongoDB Atlas via connect-mongo. Without it every post-login request 401s.

nodes.label: Public Read-Only Demo Login
nodes.rationale: Google keeps the OAuth app in Testing mode because it requests restricted gmail.readonly and calendar scopes, so only listed test users can sign in with Google; publishing would require Google verification and a security assessment. The demo login instead creates a Passport session for a synthetic user with isDemo:true and no Google token, so anyone can view the project without a Google account.

nodes.label: Secret Rotation Before Go-Live
nodes.rationale: server/.env and client/.env are committed for local dev only, so every secret (Mongo, Google OAuth, Groq) must be rotated and stored in Vercel's env UI, never in the repo.

nodes.label: Trust Proxy and Secure Cookies Behind Vercel
nodes.norm_label: trust proxy and secure cookies behind vercel
nodes.rationale: app.set("trust proxy", 1) is required behind the Vercel proxy for secure cookies to be issued correctly; omitting it produces 'Cannot set headers after they are sent' and secure-cookie-over-HTTP warnings.

nodes.label: Two-Project Vercel Architecture (saarthi-mail + saarthi-mail-api)
nodes.rationale: Frontend and backend deploy as two separate Vercel projects on default *.vercel.app subdomains so no custom domain is required; frontend is a static Vite dist build, backend is a serverless function. Custom domains later require only env var and Google Console updates, no code changes.

nodes.label: Mocked-Data-First MVP Scope
nodes.rationale: Build auth, inbox, detail, AI panel, responsive layout, and motion polish against mocked data first; backend integration and Gmail APIs are deliberately deferred so the demo-critical UI lands early.

nodes.label: Selective Glassmorphism
nodes.rationale: Glass surfaces are limited to the AI panel, auth screen, and floating controls — applying frosted blur everywhere, or using heavy shadows, dark neumorphism, or excessive gradients, would break the calm premium feel.

nodes.label: Solid Base Tile with Colored Side Faces
nodes.norm_label: solid base tile with colored side faces

nodes.label: Favicon-Scale Icon Design (33px canvas, no viewBox)
nodes.norm_label: favicon-scale icon design (33px canvas, no viewbox)

nodes.norm_label: public static web app logo asset

nodes.norm_label: alpha mask with gaussian-blurred ellipse layers

nodes.label: Accessibility Requirements
nodes.rationale: Keyboard navigation, visible focus rings, reduced-motion support, high-contrast text, and screen reader labels are required, which constrains the motion system.

nodes.label: Controlled Motion System (150ms / 300ms Framer Motion)
nodes.rationale: Motion is expressive but restricted to 150ms and 300ms durations and productivity-focused uses (sidebar, card reveal, selection, AI stagger, skeletons); bouncy, over-animated, or long transitions are avoided so the UI stays fast and calm.

nodes.label: Command Palette
nodes.rationale: Keyboard-first entry point for search, compose, navigation, archive, mark important, toggling the AI panel, and settings.
